'''Ludwig Danzer''' (15 November 1927 – 3 December 2011) was a German [[geometer]] working in [[discrete geometry]]. He was a student of [[Hanfried Lenz]], starting his career in 1960 with a thesis about "Lagerungsprobleme".<ref name=mg>{{mathgenealogy|21541}}</ref>

Danzer's name is popularized in the concepts of a [[Danzer set]], a set of points that touches all large convex sets, and the Danzer cube, an example of a non-shellable triangulation of the cube. It is an example of a power complex, studied by Danzer in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iaB3BQAAQBAJ|title=Lectures on Polytopes|last=Ziegler|first=Günter M.|date=2012-12-06|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9781461384311|language=en|contribution=Example 8.9}}</ref>

Danzer also found many new [[Aperiodic tiling|tilings]].

Ludwig Danzer worked at the [[Technical University of Dortmund]] and died on December 3, 2011,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mathematik.tu-dortmund.de/de/personen/person/Ludwig+Danzer.html|title=Personendetails - Fakultät für Mathematik, TU Dortmund|website=www.mathematik.tu-dortmund.de|access-date=2017-11-26}}
</ref> after a long illness.

Danzer had at least ten students, the most prominent one being [[Egon Schulte]].<ref name=mg/>
